summary: SIEM export (CEF) delivery & SOC2 evidence for monthly audit logs — missing rotation events and truncated entries
description:
Issue summary: Customer (GigaHealth) requested recurring monthly SIEM exports in CEF format delivered to their S3 bucket with a signed manifest and hash for SOC2 auditors. They reported two problems: (1) certain service-account rotation events are missing from the exported dataset, and (2) some events arrive truncated (payload ends with the string '[TRUNCATED]').

Impact: Customer cannot provide a complete audit trail to their auditors; SOC2 evidence deadline in two weeks. Potential regulatory impact given healthcare vertical. Affects all exported audit logs for their prod account in us-east-1 for March exports.

Customer ask: Provide immediate re-run of March export including the missing rotation events, provide signed manifest and SHA256 of the export, explain why events were truncated and confirm retention/encryption controls requested in their security questionnaire (retention window, KMS key usage, access controls, log integrity checks).

Environment: Redwood hosted (prod), customer GigaHealth account id 112233, export pipeline uses log-exporter service -> kafka -> s3-delivery lambda -> S3; CEF conversion happens in log-exporter.

Requested artifacts: sample CEF file for March 3-4, signed manifest (SHA256), export configuration for GigaHealth (filters, include_system_events), retention policy statement, KMS key id used for S3, access ACLs and IAM role used for delivery.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer submitted export request via support portal for March 1-7, format=Cef, destination=s3://gigahealth-redwood-exports, include_system_events=false

2) Support reproduced by triggering ad-hoc export for same range using internal export tool (redwoodctl export run --account 112233 --start 2026-03-03 --end 2026-03-04 --format cef --dest s3://internal-test-exports)
3) Examined resulting CEF and noticed missing events with event_type=service_account_rotation; compared against control-plane audit stream which contained the rotation events
4) Observed several heavy events (>900kB) that in CEF conversion were split and ended with '[TRUNCATED]'.

comments: 2026-03-05 09:12 - Lila Nguyen (Support): Opened ticket after customer called CS. Asked for sample CEF and manifest. Noted SOC2 deadline 2026-03-20.
2026-03-05 10:03 - Marcus Reed (SRE): Acknowledged. Will check export pipeline (kafka config + s3-delivery) and investigate filters that might exclude system events.

2026-03-05 14:21 - Michael O'Leary (GigaHealth Security): Provided their security questionnaire PDF and also attached the partial CEF they received. Confirmed missing rotation events are critical for their audit traceability.

2026-03-06 08:47 - Marcus Reed (SRE): Initial finding: export config for GigaHealth had include_system_events=false set during prior compliance parsing change (SUP-48099). This filter is excluding service_account_rotation events. Also found multiple kafka errors indicating max.message.bytes reached causing partial uploads.

2026-03-07 11:15 - Lila Nguyen (Support): Informed customer of findings and proposed two actions: (A) immediately re-run export with include_system_events=true to capture rotations and (B) temporary switch to multipart S3 delivery for large events. Customer agreed to immediate rerun.

2026-03-09 16:02 - Marcus Reed (SRE): Performed rerun to s3://redwood-temp-gigahealth-exports and uploaded signed manifest (SHA256). Observed all rotation events present. Noted ~27 events previously truncated now present as 2-part objects. Uploaded logs and manifest to ticket attachments.
2026-03-10 09:00 - Michael O'Leary (GigaHealth Security): Confirmed receipt of rerun and manifest. Asked for written confirmation of retention policy and KMS key details for evidence package.

2026-03-12 13:45 - Lila Nguyen (Support): Uploaded retention statement and KMS key metadata. Noted follow-up action to permanently fix truncation and to update the runbook. Scheduled a technical walkthrough with GigaHealth (2026-03-15).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: include_system_events filter was unintentionally set to false for this customer during a prior compliance mapping change (see SUP-48099). Verified configuration value in customer export profile: include_system_events=false.

Hypothesis 2: Kafka broker max.message.bytes default (1MB) caused large CEF-converted events to be rejected/trimmed. Observed broker logs with 'Message too large' for topic redwood-exports and corresponding s3-delivery warnings.
Evidence: Control-plane audit stream contains service_account_rotation events; those events are absent from initial export. Rerun with include_system_events=true returned the missing rotation events.

Temporary mitigation validated: rerun export to separate bucket using multipart S3 uploads preserved full payloads. Multipart path avoids kafka size constraint by streaming directly from exporter to S3 when enabled.

Longer-term: proposed infra change to log-exporter to chunk CEF conversions and stream chunks to S3 with manifest assembly; adjust kafka producer max.request.size and broker max.message.bytes for export topic; update default include_system_events to true for enterprise export profiles unless explicitly excluded.
resolution: Workaround implemented: re-ran March export with include_system_events=true and enabled multipart S3 delivery; uploaded signed manifest (SHA256) and provided to customer. Short-term fix: increased kafka producer max.request.size on log-exporter side and allowed multipart uploads for large events. Long-term plan: merge PR to implement server-side chunking and manifest assembly (see GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/log-exporter/pull/211). Runbook updates: add explicit step to verify include_system_events flag for compliance exports. Follow-ups: scheduled technical walkthrough on 2026-03-15, provide final attestation document for SOC2 by 2026-03-18, and close once customer confirms receipt to auditors.
